name: Admiral Grigorovich-class frigate (Project 11356R)

key_facts.label: Armament
key_facts.value: Vertical launch system for Kalibr, Oniks or Tsirkon cruise missiles

key_facts.label: Fleet status
key_facts.value: 3 of 6 ordered ever reached the Black Sea Fleet before Turkey closed the Straits in Feb 2022

short_role: Guided-missile frigate, the Black Sea Fleet's primary surface Kalibr launch platform
characteristics: 124.8m long, 4,000 tonnes full displacement, complement of ~200
VLS-launched Kalibr land-attack cruise missiles are the fleet's main standoff strike tool against targets deep in Ukraine
Built at Yantar Shipyard, Kaliningrad — on the Baltic, not the Black Sea, so every hull has to transit to reach its assigned fleet
Strength: Kalibr-armed surface combatant with real land-attack reach, unlike most of the rest of the Black Sea Fleet's surface units
Limitation: a surface ship, so it shares the fleet-wide exposure to Ukrainian USVs and anti-ship missiles that pushed the fleet's main basing to Novorossiysk

Estimated quantity available: 6 ordered for the Black Sea Fleet in 2010-2011; only 3 delivered before the Turkish Straits closure, the other 3 hulls diverted (two later transferred to India as the Tushil class)
employment_notes: The Black Sea Fleet's Kalibr strikes on Ukraine are launched primarily from these frigates and from the Kilo-class submarines, not from the fleet's larger but now-relocated surface combatants. Since relocating from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk, employment has shifted toward launching from further up the coast and further from Ukrainian USV range rather than forward-basing near Crimea.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional naval logistics assumed a fleet's own home port was safe rear-area infrastructure, not a target. Ukraine's drone-boat and missile campaign against Sevastopol forced a wartime relocation of an entire fleet's main base — the doctrine.md finding that control of the immediate sky and sea, not distance from the front alone, now sets where an asset can safely sit applies just as much to a naval base as it does to a SAM battery or an artillery position.
